research_question: Can an explicitly posterior-component-conditioned bounded residual reduce cross-identity predicted-gate worst-combination NMAE more reliably than the frozen shared mean residual, without changing recognition?
scientific_rationale: P3o-I falsified a global equal-weight compound-CVaR loss: it improved the selected hard group versus F but was consistently worse than the shared mean residual. P3o-J changes the information pathway rather than the CVaR weight: detached six-label posterior components select an additive 6x12 residual correction on top of the same shared delay residual.

methods.J0_shared_mean: P3o-I finite-valid state-preserving bounded shared delay residual, trained with mean masked Smooth-L1 only.
methods.J1_component_conditioned: Exactly J0 plus a learned 6x12 correction selected by the detached six-label sigmoid posterior. The correction is bounded jointly with the shared residual; no true label, target, threshold, or development statistic enters inference. Classification base is frozen and remains in eval mode.

training.calibration: F-only calibration and threshold reused verbatim by J0/J1

primary_comparison: J1 versus J0; F-base is retained as an external anchor. No CVaR fraction or weight is present.
decision_rule: Only all gates across the three fixed seeds permit generation of exactly the 1470M confirmation. Any exception, non-finite result, missing receipt, or gate failure freezes P3o-J. No rerun, tune, recalibration, threshold selection, checkpoint selection, or confirmation may use 1450M/1460M after development access.
